correctness.rationale: The universal theorem reduces to the six fully enumerated rank-four type identities and a published connected-cycle threshold, with disjoint-union congruence proved by an Ehrenfeucht strategy. The minimum is confirmed by exact exhaustive enumeration of every 105 disconnected two-regular graph on fewer than eighteen vertices against all nine connected-cycle rank-four theories. Python and C++ implement independent exhaustive type recursions, and a separate direct game minimax verifies the central witness; each program was run from the packaged paths. Finite computations do not purport to prove the infinite statement alone.

value.rationale: A sharp minimal connectivity-indistinguishability witness at fixed logical rank is a natural quantitative invariant for the classical nondefinability of connectedness. The eighteen-vertex threshold is not supplied by standard connected-cycle results and the infinite multi-component collapse is a structural extension. The precise minimum can anchor small-model and logical-complexity comparisons; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere scripted enumeration.
